#en:
I used to think the armor would make it easier to breathe. Funny how you can wear three layers of composite plating and still feel naked when someone drops a crate behind you. Today in the hangar, a loader slammed into its stops and I almost drew on it. Karina saw the flinch, pretended she did not. Later, she "casually" mentioned noise discipline drills, like that would sand down nerves that burned in years ago.

We got another briefing about the Vector contract. Command says it is just overwatch, pattern analysis, low-risk escort while some client chases ghosts in the lanes. Marcus does not buy it. He pointed out that every time a ship touches those routes, insurance rates spike and the paperwork comes through half-redacted. Nadia swears she saw UC tags buried in the metadata on our last packet. Nobody says it out loud, but it feels like we are walking between blades again, hired to stand in the space where bigger knives might cross.

I keep thinking about leaving. I have packed my duffel three times in as many years. Every time, someone from upstairs calls me in, lays out new pay scales, lighter rotations, "cleaner" jobs. Once they even mentioned a consultancy slot, no fieldwork. Within days, the inbox fills with the same old ops, just with different codenames and hazard bonuses tagged on. So I stay, jumpy at every bang and shadow, watching people like Karina and Marcus measure distances in escape vectors instead of meters, and pretending this is still just a job.
zh:
我以前以为穿上装甲会让人呼吸更容易些。有趣的是，你穿着三层复合装甲板，还是会在有人在你身后丢下货箱时觉得自己赤身裸体。今天在机库里，一台装卸机撞上限位，我差点朝它拔枪。卡琳娜看见了那一下瑟缩，假装没看见。后来她"随口"提起噪声纪律操演，仿佛那能磨平多年前就烧进神经的紧张。

我们又接到一次关于"向量"合同的简报。指挥部说那只是监视、模式分析、低风险护航，某个客户在航道里追鬼而已。马库斯不信。他指出每次有飞船碰到那些航线，保险费率就飙升，文书送过来时总有一半被涂黑。娜迪亚赌咒说她在我们上一份数据包的元数据里看到了埋藏的联殖标签。没人说出口，但感觉我们又走在了刀刃之间，被雇来站在几把更大的刀可能交叉的地方。

我总想着离开。三年里我打了三次行囊。每次楼上就有人把我叫去，抛出新的薪酬等级、更轻的轮班、"更干净"的活儿。有一次他们甚至提到一个顾问岗位，不用出外勤。可几天之内，收件箱就又塞满了同样那些旧任务，只是换了个代号、加了个危险津贴。于是我留下，对每一声闷响和每一道影子都一惊一乍，看着卡琳娜和马库斯这样的人用逃生矢量而不是米来丈量距离，并假装这仍然只是一份工作。

#en:
I used to write dates at the top of these, like that made anything official. Time is just burn and cooling metal out here, so what is the point.  

There was a stretch, right after the ring, where I could not sleep without hearing the collision in my head. Alarms, metal screaming, all of it layered over the memory of me, days earlier, pointing at the numbers and saying this will fail. At first I carried that like a broken rib I did not want anyone to see. After a while, the ache just became background noise. You learn to breathe around it.  

Funny thing: once the guilt went dull, the hesitation went with it. I stopped flinching at the idea that something I built might crack a hull, or that a drone I reprogrammed might miss a warning buoy. They already decided I was the problem, so why not become the variable they cannot control.  

This new yard, strung through forgotten metal where no one bothers to look, makes sense for a lot of reasons. Scrap is cheap, eyes are fewer, and every dead freighter is a lesson in where the big powers decided a life was not worth a repair ticket. I weld over their decisions, brace their failures, and sell the result to people who at least know what they are buying.  

What scares me is not being caught. It is being paraded. Some tribunal on Jemison, some carefully edited feed where I sit in a cage while they pretend this was one woman with a torch, not decades of cuts and lies. I will burn every bridge I have before I give them that.
zh:
我以前会在这些开头写上日期，像那样就能让它变得正式。在这外面，时间只是点火和冷却的金属，那又有什么意义。

有一段时间，就在那个环之后，我不听到碰撞声在脑子里回响就睡不着。警报、金属的尖叫，全都叠在我几天前指着那些数字说"这会失败"的记忆上。起初我像带着一根断肋一样扛着它，不想让任何人看见。过了一阵，那痛就变成了背景噪声。你学会绕着它呼吸。

有趣的是：愧疚一变得迟钝，犹豫也跟着没了。我不再因为想到自己造的东西可能让船壳开裂、或我重编的无人机可能错过一个警告浮标而畏缩。他们早就认定我是问题，那为什么不干脆成为他们控制不了的变量。

这个新船坞穿在被遗忘的金属之间、没人费心去看的地方，有很多理由说得通。废料便宜，眼睛更少，而每一艘死货船都是一课，教人看清大势力在哪里认定一条命不值得一张维修单。我在他们的决定上焊接，给他们的失败加固，然后把成品卖给至少清楚自己在买什么的人。

让我害怕的不是被抓住。是被示众。杰米森上某个法庭，某段精心剪辑的直播，我坐在笼子里，而他们假装这只是一个拿着割枪的女人，而不是几十年的削减与谎言。要我把这个交给他们，我宁可把我所有的桥都烧了。

#en:
I have been staring at dead screens in this rock for six months, so when one of them blinked tonight, I thought I was finally losing it.

We were supposed to be monitoring routine traffic, cataloging the usual noise; instead I found a sliver of an old ops file tucked behind a corrupted index. Half the headers are scrubbed, timestamps misaligned, but the pattern underneath is wrong in the same way as that stray dataslate we pulled off the abandoned outpost. Same cluster of derelict IDs. Same "administrative closures" on ships that never sent final manifests. And threaded through it, a repeated arbitration tag tied to someone who should not exist on UC channels at all.

The story in the mess is that years back there was a case that went bad, some arbitrator who signed the wrong ruling and vanished. Depending who you ask, she died in the blast, ran with a hold full of stolen cores, or got buried on a black payroll. Nobody remembers the original version, just a handful of contradictions that all start sounding like myth if you drink enough.

This fragment does not give me a name, but it does give me a path. The routing note points forward to an old listening post that was never formally decommissioned, just quietly taken off the books, the way you close your eyes and pretend the noise stopped. First clue from the outpost was dismissed as a glitch; now the decrypted file echoes it, and both point toward that silent station where someone thought no one would ever look again.
zh:
我在这块岩石里盯着死掉的屏幕六个月了，所以今晚其中一块眨了一下时，我以为自己终于疯了。

我们本该监控例行交通、给寻常噪声编目；结果我却在一条损坏的索引后面找到了一份旧作战文件的碎片。一半页眉被擦掉，时间戳错位，可底下的图案和那块我们从废弃前哨站取下的游离数据板一样不对劲。同一簇弃船 ID。同样那些从未发出最终清单的飞船的"行政结案"。而贯穿其中的，是一个反复出现的仲裁标签，绑在某个本不该出现在联殖频道上的人身上。

食堂里的故事是，多年前有个案子办砸了，某个仲裁者签错了裁决，然后消失了。取决于你问谁，她要么死在爆炸里，要么带着满满一舱偷来的核心跑了，要么被埋进了一份秘密薪酬名单。没人记得最初的版本，只有一堆自相矛盾之处——只要你喝得够多，它们就都开始像神话。

这份碎片没给我名字，但给了我一条路。那条航路备注指向一座从未正式退役、只是被悄悄从记录里划掉的旧监听站——就像你闭上眼睛假装噪声停了。前哨站的第一条线索当时被当成故障驳回；如今这份解密文件与它呼应，两者都指向那座沉默的空间站，有人以为再也不会有人去看的地方。

#en:
Recording this so if anyone digs OM-2098 out of her patrol loop and wonders how we missed it, they will know it was not one big conspiracy. Just a thousand little shrugs.

We got the revised manifest three days ago. Deimos hull IDs, nothing special, routine salvage oversight request. Ops flagged a checksum mismatch, but the watch officer said the system was "still syncing to central" and cleared it. I meant to follow up. Shift change hit, my relief was late, and by the time I handed the console over I had talked myself into believing him.

Next rotation, I noticed a courier entry buried under generic scrap classifications. UC science tag, old but not that old. I pinged for clarification. The reply came back from a junior clerk planet-side, canned language about decommission backlogs and a reminder about our queue. I asked Elena to take a second look at the routing codes. She nodded, said she would, then got pulled into a call with command. I never saw the result.

It feels different now, looking back. One missing annotation here, one misrouted query there, a night where I skipped logging a gut feeling because the air was too stale and my head hurt from grav-cycling glitches. None of it big enough to halt a Navy ship. All of it pointed the same direction, if anyone had taken the time to draw a line.

If this log survives and you are listening from some dead yard over Deimos, know this: we did not ignore the cracks. We just kept assuming someone else was already patching them.
zh:
录下这个，好让将来有人把 OM-2098 从她的巡逻循环里挖出来、琢磨我们怎么会漏掉时，他们会知道那不是一场大阴谋。只是一千次小小的耸肩。

三天前我们收到修订版清单。火卫二的船体 ID，没什么特别的，例行打捞监管申请。作战部标出了一处校验和不符，可值班军官说系统"还在与中枢同步"，就放行了。我本打算跟进。换班时间到了，接班的人来晚了，等我把控制台交出去时，我已经说服自己相信了他。

下一轮轮班，我注意到一条埋在通用废料分类底下的快船条目。联殖科学标签，旧，但没那么旧。我发消息要求澄清。回复来自行星表面一个初级文员，是些关于退役积压的套话，外加一句提醒我们排队。我让埃琳娜再看一眼那些航路代码。她点头，说会看，然后被叫去和指挥部通了个话。结果我始终没见过。

回头看，现在感觉不一样了。这里少一条注释，那里一次把查询发错了地方，一个夜里我因为空气太陈旧、脑袋又因重力循环故障而疼，就跳过了记录一次直觉。没有一样大到足以叫停一艘海军飞船。可如果有人花时间画条线，它们全都指向同一个方向。

如果这份日志还在，而你在火卫二上方某座死船坞里听着，请记住：我们没有无视那些裂缝。我们只是一直在想当然地以为已经有别人在补了。

#en:
I was never supposed to be on a Navy hull. Freight, sure. Charter runs, maybe. But steel with that emblem on the bulkhead? That belonged to people who knew what they were doing. Then one bad harvest on a dusty rock and a recruiter with a clean smile, and somehow I am strapped into PX-7708 listening to officers argue over approach vectors.

We have been running close to the storms for weeks now. First it was because the corridor was "temporarily congested." Then because some governor wanted relief supplies yesterday. Now the story is that our numbers are so clean we would be wasting fuel not using them. Funny how necessity always starts sounding like habit.

The crew talks in half-whispers when the duty lights dim. Someone mentioned settlers out along a narrow lane near Akila who swear a ghost pilot threads their shipments through dust like it is nothing. Another swears they saw the same signature buried in our course corrections, just a flicker in the logs. I do not know what scares me more, that they might be right or that I am starting to hope we have someone like that watching over us.

I keep thinking about that abandoned lab we passed weeks back, the one we were told not to log hull-side. Beacons spitting lies into the sky, ships following numbers they never meant to trust. Maybe that is all any of us are doing now, inch by inch. We did not set out to cut this close. We just kept shaving the margin until there was nothing left between us and whatever waits in those storms.
zh:
我本不该上一艘海军飞船。货运，没问题。包机航次，也许。可舱壁上挂着那个徽记的钢铁？那属于懂行的人。然后一块满是灰尘的岩石上歉收了一季，来了个笑容干净的招募员，不知怎的我就在 PX-7708 上系好安全带，听军官们为进近矢量争论。

我们已经贴着风暴跑了好几周了。起初是因为那条走廊"临时拥堵"。后来是因为某个总督昨天就要救援物资。现在说法变成了我们的数字太干净，不用就浪费燃料。有趣的是，必要性总会开始听起来像习惯。

值勤灯一暗，船员们就用半声耳语说话。有人提到阿基拉附近一条窄航道上的定居者，他们赌咒说有个幽灵飞行员把他们的货运像没事一样穿过尘暴。另一个人赌咒说在我们自己的航向修正里看到同样的特征，只是日志里的一闪。我不知道哪个更让我害怕：是他们也许说对了，还是我开始希望真有这么个人在照看我们。

我总想起几周前我们路过的那座废弃实验室——那座他们叫我们不要在船体日志里记录。信标朝天吐着谎言，飞船跟着一些它们本不该信任的数字走。也许这现在就是我们所有人都在做的事，一寸一寸地。我们并非一开始就打算切得这么近。我们只是一直削减余量，直到我们和风暴里等待的东西之间什么都不剩。

#en:
I am putting this down on a throwaway slate because saying it out loud in the bar would get me laughed at, or worse, remembered.

Couple days back I took a short-haul contract out past the usual freight spine, nothing fancy, just hauling nutrient and polymer to a LIST outpost. Midway through, the ship chirped with a course correction that did not come from my filed plan. No beacon ID, just a quiet nudge, like the autopilot suddenly remembered a better idea. I checked the math. It was good. Too good. Shaved six minutes off the run, slid us between a clutter of old traffic like it had been choreographed.

At the outpost they swore my arrival time matched their manifest exactly. No surprise. No delay. Like somebody had pre-written the coincidence.

Since then I have heard similar stories in Gagarin and Neon: freighters that arrive early with no one willing to swear to why, convoys that drop off scans entirely and then show up clean two jumps later. Every time someone starts to say it out loud, you can see them tap the brakes on their own words, make a joke, change the subject. Out here, anyone who sounds too certain about invisible hands on the lanes suddenly finds themselves short on work and long on scrutiny.

I do not know if there is really a man behind those corrections or just a pattern we are all leaning into because it is easier than admitting we fly half-blind. I just know the vectors are not random, and whoever is drawing them understands my routes better than I ever did.
zh:
我把这个记在一块用完就扔的数据板上，因为在酒吧里大声说出来会让我被人笑话，或者更糟——被人记住。

几天前我接了一份短途合同，跑出惯常的货运主干道，没什么讲究，只是把营养剂和聚合物运到一座独立盟前哨站。半路上，飞船滴了一声，给出一条不属于我申报计划的航向修正。没有信标 ID，只有一声安静的轻推，像自动驾驶忽然想起了更好的主意。我核对了算式。它很好。太好了。把航程削掉了六分钟，让我们滑过一堆旧交通，像编排过一样。

在前哨站，他们赌咒说我的抵达时间与他们的清单分毫不差。没有意外。没有延误。像有人预先写好了这个巧合。

从那以后，我在加加林和霓虹城听到过类似的故事：提前抵达、没人肯赌咒说为什么的货船；整个从扫描上消失、两个跃迁后又干干净净出现的运输队。每次有人开始大声说出来，你就能看到他给自己的话踩了刹车，开个玩笑，换个话题。在这外面，任何对航道上的看不见的手显得太确定的人，会突然发现自己活儿变少、被盯着看变多。

我不知道那些修正背后是不是真有一个男人，还是只是一个我们都在迎合的图案，因为迎合比承认自己是半瞎飞行的更容易。我只知道那些矢量不是随机的，而画它们的人对我的航线，比我曾经懂得的还要清楚。

#en:
I thought this posting would be quiet. A place to age out my contract with bad coffee and routine patrol schedules, maybe write up a few spacer disputes and call it duty. Instead I am drowning in other people's weather.

They come in waves. Farmhands with sunburned faces, freighter captains still smelling of coolant, one LIST rep who looked like she had not slept in a week. They argue about what they saw out there, always starting with something small. A storm that arrived hours early. A squall that parted just wide enough for one ship and then slammed shut on the escorts. A transponder that winked out precisely when the ion readings spiked.

I string their accounts up on the wall because there is nowhere else to put them. At first it was just to keep them straight in my head, a way to prove to myself it was all coincidence. But the pins kept landing in the same rough arc, across different systems, different months, different insurance forms that all said the same thing in nicer language: unavoidable conditions.

What no one mentions unless they forget I am listening is the pilot. Always the same shape of her, even when the details change. Quiet. Watches the sky more than the room. Talks like she learned Standard late and still thinks in another tongue. Pays in full, but leaves as soon as the clouds start building.

Looking at this wall now, I cannot tell if we missed her for years because the pattern was too small, or because none of us really wanted to admit the storms might have a favorite.
zh:
我以为这个岗位会很安静。一个用来消磨合同期的地方，就着烂咖啡和例行巡逻表，或许再写几份太空人纠纷的记录，就叫尽忠职守了。结果我却淹没在别人的天气里。

他们一波一波地来。脸庞晒伤的农工、身上还带着冷却液味的货船船长、一个看起来一周没睡的独立盟代表。他们争论着自己在那外面看到了什么，总是从一件小事讲起。一场提前数小时到来的风暴。一道刚好裂开够一艘船通过、随后又对护航船猛地合拢的狂风带。一个恰好在电离读数飙升时熄掉的应答器。

我把他们的叙述钉在墙上，因为没别处可放。起初只是为了在脑子里理清，向自己证明那全是巧合。可那些图钉总是落在同一道粗略的弧线上——跨越不同的星系、不同的月份、不同的保险单，而那些保险单都用更好听的措辞说着同一件事：不可避免的条件。

有一件事，除非他们忘了我还在听，没人会提起——那个飞行员。哪怕细节在变，她的轮廓总是一样。安静。看天空的时间比看室内多。说话像她很晚才学会通用语、还用另一种语言思考。全额付款，可云一开始堆积就走。

如今看着这面墙，我分不清我们多年来漏了她，是因为图案太小，还是因为我们没人真愿意承认，风暴也许也有偏爱。
